How NBME words questions

Patterns seen on the NBME form questions logged so far. Each line gives one paraphrased example and the brief that shows it.

  1. The diagnosis is given as its mechanism. A toddler with hip dysplasia found late is keyed as a poorly developed acetabulum, and a newborn with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency as an enzyme deficiency. The Limping Child
  2. The organism is asked as a class. A painless genital ulcer is keyed as a spirochete, with obligate intracellular bacterium and gram-negative diplococcus beside it. Genital Ulcer: Painless or Painful
  3. A disease appears under a formal or older name. Kawasaki disease is listed as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome, usually as a decoy. Acute Rheumatic Fever
  4. A decoy shares a name with a disease that would fit. Fanconi syndrome, a kidney tubule disorder, is offered among marrow failures; Fanconi anemia is the disease that would fit. Recurrent Abscesses and Granulomas
  5. The genetic defect and the parent of origin replace the syndrome. Angelman syndrome is keyed as a chromosome 15 deletion inherited from the mother, with the same deletion from the father as the next option. Angelman Syndrome and Its Genetic Look-Alikes
  6. The key is a procedure or a way of measuring. Protein on a routine dipstick in a well adolescent is keyed as a repeat urinalysis at bedtime and on waking; a high automated blood pressure is keyed as a measurement by auscultation. Incidental Proteinuria in a Well Child
  7. An exposure is planted as bait. Cat scratches sit beside a cat-scratch disease option when the key is an infected thyroglossal duct cyst, and mosquito bites sit in a spotted fever stem. A refugee camp is different: it is a real risk factor for rheumatic fever, and it also invites travel-fever decoys. Enlarged Lymph Nodes: Reading the Pattern
  8. Development comes as a grid. Each option is a row of delayed or normal for gross motor, fine motor and language, so every domain in the stem has to be read on its own. Growth & Developmental Milestones
  9. The lead-in grants part of the answer. A bleeding newborn is asked what to give in addition to vitamin K, which leaves only the blood product to choose. Fat-Soluble Vitamin Deficiency and Toxicity
  10. A definition may be dated. Older sources, including this NBME explanation, set adolescent hypertension at the 95th percentile at every age. The current 2017 American Academy of Pediatrics guideline uses a fixed cutoff of 130/80 mm Hg from age 13. Confirming High Blood Pressure in an Adolescent
